# Alan Dale Telfer (1890–1937)

**Born:** 27 Oct 1890 (Tantanoola, SA) | **Died:** 13 Sep 1937 (Wilga Tank, Girilambone, NSW) | **Mother:** [[Martha Clara Henstridge (1854–1921)]] | **Father:** [[John Telfer (1840–1913)]] | **Occupation:** Coalminer / Ganger (railway labor) | **Buried:** Unknown (Girilambone district)

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|---|---|
| Self | Alan Dale Telfer |
| Father | [[John Telfer (1840–1913)]] |
| Mother | Martha Clara Henstridge |
| Siblings | [[James Telfer (1866–1946)]], Elizabeth Telfer (Clarke), Susan Telfer (Agnew), Martha Telfer (Cameron), [[Mark Telfer (1877–1946)]], Maria Clara Telfer, Isabella Lucieton Telfer (Thomson), John Roland Telfer, Clara Blanche Telfer (Lane), Robert Freddy Telfer, Douglas Telfer, Colin Roy Telfer, Alma Tressy Telfer (Cullen), [[Marian Telfer Cornish (1896–1977)]] |

## Life Summary

Alan Dale Telfer was born on 27 October 1890 in Tantanoola, South Australia, the 13th child of John Telfer (1840–1913) and his second wife Martha Clara Henstridge.

He never married. During the Great Depression of the 1920s-1930s, Alan migrated far from the agricultural safety of South Australia's Limestone Coast to the interior of New South Wales. He found work as a **ganger** (railway labor foreman) and **coalminer** — a gruelling and highly itinerant profession that took him deep into the state's central-west.

### Death — Resolved (NSW Government Gazette)

Alan's fate was a long-standing mystery in the Telfer family tree. The resolution came via an NSW Government Gazette intestate estate notice, which confirmed:

> Alan Dale Telfer, late of **Wilga Tank, Girilambone**, in the State of New South Wales, died **intestate** on **13 September 1937**.

Girilambone and the associated Wilga Tank area was a remote railway siding and copper mining outpost in central-western New South Wales. His death there, without a will, paints a picture of a rugged, transient, and likely impoverished life in his final years — a stark contrast to the settled farming life of his Tantanoola siblings.

His exact burial location is unknown but likely in the Girilambone district.

## Timeline

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| 27 Oct 1890 | Born at Tantanoola, South Australia |
| 5 Jan 1913 | Father John Telfer died at Tantanoola |
| ~1920s–1930s | Migrated to New South Wales for railway and mining work |
| 13 Nov 1921 | Mother Martha Clara Henstridge died at Adelaide |
| 13 Sep 1937 | Died intestate at Wilga Tank, Girilambone, NSW |

## Notes

- **Mystery resolved (2026):** Alan's death was listed as "Unknown" in the vault until the NSW Government Gazette intestate notice was found via Gemini Deep Research. The approved report (Skippy ✅ 29 May 2026) confirmed the 13 Sep 1937 date and Girilambone location.
- **Occupation:** Listed as "ganger" — a railway labor foreman responsible for a gang of track workers. This fits the Girilambone location, which was a railway siding on the Nyngan–Cobar line.
- **Never married:** Unlike most of his siblings, Alan never married and had no known children.
- **1964 date artifact:** Like his brothers Colin Roy and John Roland, some digital indexes incorrectly attributed the 4 Aug 1964 death date of his half-sister Martha Cameron to Alan. This has been disproven.

- **Father:** John Laurie (born 1 May 1737, Auchtermuchty, Fife — died 1795)
- **Mother:** Elizabeth Low (1739–1810)
- **Married:** 7 December 1769, Auchtermuchty, Fife, Scotland

## Grandparents (John Laurie's parents)
- **Paternal Grandfather:** John Lourie (born c.1689)
- **Paternal Grandmother:** Ann Gilmour (born c.1697)
- **Married:** Auchtermuchty, Fife

- Jean Dunlop's parents are also worth researching — she was born c.1791, likely in Ayrshire

## Timeline

| Date | Event |
|---|---|

| 13 Nov 1921 | Mother Martha Clara Henstridge died |
| 8 May 1976 | Died at Ringwood, Victoria (age 83) |

## Notes

- **Death found:** 8 May 1976, Ringwood, Victoria, age 83. Confirmed via RootsWeb family card showing George Lewis Cullen & Alma Tressie Telfer — "5 Sep 1923, Renmark, SA, age: 31" and "8 May 1976, Ringwood, Vic, age: 83".
- **Marriage date corrected:** The RootsWeb source records the marriage as 5 Sep 1923 in Renmark SA (not 3 Jan 1921 at Tantanoola as previously recorded). This later marriage at age 31 (rather than 27) and in Renmark rather than Tantanoola needs verification against the original SA marriage index.
- **Interstate migration:** Died in Ringwood, Victoria (outer eastern Melbourne suburb). This explains why her death was not found in South Australian records — she moved to Victoria after marriage.
- **Marriage vs mother's death:** Original research noted she married "just months before her mother's death in late 1921" — with the corrected 1923 marriage date, the timeline changes significantly. Her mother died in November 1921, and Alma married nearly two years later in Renmark.

# Caroline Amelia Telfer (née Masters)

**Role:** Mark's great-great-grandmother — English immigrant
**Born:** 10 June 1842 — Tiffield, Northamptonshire, England
**Died:** 24 August 1929 — Clare, South Australia (within hours of her husband)
**Buried:** Clare Cemetery, Clare, South Australia
**Arrival:** *Templar* — arrived Port Adelaide, 24 November 1845 (aged 3)

## Life Story

Caroline Amelia Masters was born on **10 June 1842** in the village of **Tiffield, Northamptonshire, England**. She was just three years old when her family emigrated to South Australia aboard the **Templar**, arriving at Port Adelaide on **24 November 1845**.

Her father **Charles Masters** (1809–1866) was a farmer who established "Wroxton Grange" near Angaston, South Australia, and was a noted horse breeder. He died in 1866 of liver complications and was buried at Angaston Old Cemetery.

On **22 September 1874**, Caroline married **John Telfer** at the Baptist Chapel, Tarlee. Together they raised **six sons** at Willow Plains, near Clare, where they lived for 47 years.

### The Tragic Conclusion

In a remarkable and poignant end to a long marriage, Caroline died **within hours** of her husband John in August 1929. John passed away on **23 August 1929**, and Caroline followed him the next day, **24 August 1929**. The *Register News-Pictorial* (Adelaide) ran a photograph captioned:

> "THE LATE MRS. JOHN TELFER, of Clare, who died within a few hours of her husband. Both were prominent Clare residents."

They are buried together at **Clare Cemetery, South Australia**.

## Life Summary

Caroline Edna Lawrie was born in 1890 in the Gilbert district of South Australia, the daughter of **Robert Dunlop Lawrie** and **Caroline Hosking**. Her father was a farmer in the Long Plains / Balaklava district.

She married **[[William Henry Parker (1893–1968)]]** on 29 March 1917 in South Australia. William Henry was a farmer from the Long Plains area, son of [[William Humphrey Parker (1850–1926)]] and [[Hannah Parker (1855–1948)]].

They had **five children**: Avis, Howard Lindsay, Sydney Hugh, William Humphrey, and **[[Shirley Edna Telfer (1929–2017)|Shirley Edna Parker]]** (your grandmother).

**Notable family connection:** Caroline's brother **Frank Lindsay Lawrie** (1886–1920) married **Sophia Parker** — William Henry's sister — creating a sibling swap between the Lawrie and Parker families.

Caroline died in 1957.

---

## The Lawrie Line

Robert Dunlop Lawrie was the son of **John Lawrie** and **Janet Lawrie** (per Geni records). The Lawrie name is Scottish in origin — likely from Ayrshire or Renfrewshire — though Robert's parents' origins are still being researched.

Robert and Caroline (Hosking) Lawrie had at least 7 children:
- Jephthah Robert Lawrie (1878–1961)
- Charles Alexander Lawrie (1881–1969)
- Ernest William Lawrie (1883–1966)
- Ellen Christina (McLaughlin) (1885–1972)
- Frank Lindsay Lawrie (1886–1920)
- **Caroline Edna (Parker)** (1890–1957)
- Margaret Isabel (Agars) (1896–1976)

Robert died in 1917 and is buried at Shannon Cemetery, Long Plains. Caroline Hosking died in 1920.

# Caroline Hosking (1851–1920)

## Basic Details
- **Full Name:** Caroline Hosking
- **Born:** 6 May 1851, New Cumnock, Ayrshire, Scotland (FamilySearch, Geni — multiple independent trees)
- **Alternative birth year:** c.1862 (per death notice saying "aged 58" in Dec 1920)
- **Birthplace:** New Cumnock, Ayrshire, Scotland (FamilySearch, Geni — multiple independent trees)
- **Death:** 29 December 1920, Long Plains, South Australia (per Trove death notice)
- **Death (alternative):** Some records say 5 January 1920 (Geni, FamilySearch) — death notice in Trove (Observer, 10 Jan 1920, p.27) confirms "29th December" as primary source
- **Age at Death:** 69 (if born 1851) — though death notice says "aged 58" (suggests birth c.1862); discrepancy unresolved
- **Burial:** Shannon/Calomba Cemetery, South Australia — Section SE 33, Plot 68, buried 07/01/1920
- **Marriage:** Robert Dunlop Lawrie (1850–1917), about 1879 in South Australia

## Parents (CONFIRMED from FamilySearch catalog)
- **Father:** Thomas Hosking (1821–1854)
  - Born: 1821, St Columb Major, Cornwall
  - Died: 1854, Burra, South Australia (miner)
  - Occupation: Miner (copper mines at Burra)
- **Mother:** Catherine May (1817–1908)
  - Born: c.1817, possibly St Keverne, Cornwall (though not found in St Keverne baptism records 1800-1857)
  - Died: 1908, Long Plains, South Australia (per Trove death notice 28 Aug 1920 — Catherine Hosking)
  - NOTE: Catherine Hosking died 28 Aug 1920 (Trove article 89186299 — "HOSKING" notice)

## Immigration
- Thomas Hosking (1821–1854) and Catherine May (1817–1908) immigrated to South Australia in **1847**
- Ship: Not yet confirmed. Searched "La Belle Alliance" (arr. 2 Jul 1847) — no Hosking listed on WikiTree passenger profiles. Searched "Santipore" (arr. 1848) — a Facebook post mentions a different Thomas Hosking arriving on this ship in 1848.
- The SA "Passengers in History" database (passengers.history.sa.gov.au) has an entry for Thomas Hosking, age 20, Miner — likely the 1821-1854 Thomas
- Further research needed on the exact ship

## Paternal Grandparents (Thomas Hosking 1821-1854's parents)
- From FamilySearch catalog entry #672924 ("Hosking family history"):
  - **Thomas Hosking (1764–1798)** — born in Botus Fleming, Cornwall
  - **Parents of Thomas Hosking (1764-1798):** John Hosking and Joan Smith
  - This Thomas (1764-1798) was the grandfather of Thomas Hosking (1821-1854)
  - The father of Thomas Hosking (1821-1854) is not named in the catalog entry but would be the son of Thomas (1764-1798)

## Children (from Geni — Robert Dunlop Lawrie profile, 10 children total)
| Name | Birth Date | Birthplace |
|------|------------|------------|
| Catherine Leah Lawrie | 23 March 1880 | Dublin, South Australia |
| Janet Stevenson Lawrie | 19 May 1881 | Dublin, South Australia |
| Alberta Grace Lawrie | 4 September 1882 | Long Plains, South Australia |
| Hugh John Lawrie | 24 July 1885 | Balaklava, South Australia |
| Frank Lindsay Lawrie | 27 December 1886 | Balaklava, South Australia |
| Jeanette Lawrie | 1887 | (not specified) |
| Marion Vida Lawrie | 23 May 1888 | Alma, South Australia |
| Caroline Edna Lawrie | 21 April 1890 | Balaklava, South Australia |
| Robert Dunlop Lawrie (Jr.) | 18 June 1891 | Long Plains, South Australia |

## Death Notices
- **Caroline Lawrie died 29 Dec 1920, age 58:**
  - "LAWRIE.—On the 29th December, at the residence of her son-in-law (Mr. James Davey), Long Plains, Caroline, widow of the late Robert Dunlop Lawrie, aged 58 years."
  - Source: Observer (Adelaide, SA), 10 Jan 1920, Page 27
  - https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/165672457
- **Catherine Hosking (her mother) died 28 Aug 1920:**
  - Source: The Express and Telegraph (Adelaide, SA), 28 Aug 1920, Page 2
  - https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/89186299

- **Geni (Caroline Hosking — parents, siblings):** https://www.geni.com/people/Caroline-Hosking/6000000001359630055
- **FamilySearch (Alexander Lawrie — shows Caroline as daughter-in-law):** https://ancestors.familysearch.org/en/LZ12-XRS/alexander-lawrie-1780-1847
- **FamilySearch Catalog (Hosking family history):** https://www.familysearch.org/en/search/catalog/672924
  - Describes "Thomas Hosking (1764-1798), son of John and Joan Smith Hosking was born in Botus Fleming, Cornwall. His grandson, Thomas Hosking (1821-1854) married Catherine May (1817-1908) and immigrated to South Australia in 1847."
- **Geni (Alexander Lawrie I — shows Caroline as daughter-in-law):** https://www.geni.com/people/Alexander-Lawrie-I/6000000001358151294
- **WikiTree (Lawrie-15 — Robert Dunlop Lawrie profile):** https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Lawrie-15
- **Carnamah Bio (Alberta Grace Lawrie):** https://www.carnamah.com.au/bio/alberta-grace-lawrie
- **Passengers in History (SA):** https://passengers.history.sa.gov.au/node/685267 (Thomas Hosking, miner, age 20)
- **FindAGrave (Robert Dunlop Lawrie):** https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/201872053/robert_dunlop_lawrie
- **St Keverne Baptisms (checked 1800-1857):** http://www.st-keverne.com/history/records/bapt_1800-1857.php
  - No "May" surname found among baptisms, suggesting Catherine May may have been born elsewhere or not Church of England baptized

# Elizabeth Beattie Telfer (1832–1896)

**Born:** 1832–1834, Kelso, Roxburghshire, Scottish Borders, Scotland | **Died:** 17 February 1896, Norwood, SA (age 62–64) | **Mother:** [[Elizabeth Beattie (1802–1891)]] | **Father:** [[James Telfer (1796–1863)]] | **Occupation:** Wife, mother, pioneer | **Burial:** Houghton Cemetery, section E, row 11, site 377

> Also known as Elizabeth Beattie Dillon after marriage. A Scottish immigrant who arrived in 1854 on the *Oliver Lang* with her brothers James and Robert, travelled overland from Melbourne to South Australia.

## Life Summary

Elizabeth Beattie Telfer was born in Kelso, Roxburghshire, Scottish Borders, Scotland, likely around 1832–1834, the daughter of James Telfer (1796–1863) and Elizabeth Beattie (1802–1891). She grew up in the rural Scottish borderlands, a region known for sheep farming and textile weaving.

In 1854, at approximately age 20–22, Elizabeth immigrated to Australia on the ship *Oliver Lang* with her brothers James and Robert. The ship landed in Melbourne, and the siblings travelled overland to South Australia, where they visited her uncle Francis Telfer at "Macoota," Kersbrook.

On **18 December 1856**, Elizabeth married **John Charles Dillon** at the residence of Francis Telfer, Chain of Ponds, South Australia. The marriage was registered at Talunga, SA, Volume 8, Page 376.

Between 1858 and 1871, Elizabeth bore nine children at their home in the Para Wirra / Chain of Ponds district. The family was deeply connected to the Mount Lofty Ranges — John Charles Dillon acquired land sections 648, 5517, and 5521 in the Hundred of Para Wirra in 1860 under the new Torrens Title system.

Elizabeth passed away on 17 February 1896 in Norwood, SA (age 62), and was buried at Houghton Cemetery. Her husband John survived her by a decade, dying in 1906 at Tea Tree Gully.

## Life Summary

Elizabeth Beattie Telfer was born in Kelso, Roxburghshire, Scottish Borders, Scotland, likely around 1832–1834, the daughter of James Telfer (1796–1863) and Elizabeth Beattie (1802–1891). She grew up in the rural Scottish borderlands, a region known for sheep farming and textile weaving.

In 1854, at approximately age 20–22, Elizabeth immigrated to Australia on the ship *Oliver Lang* with her brothers James and Robert. The ship landed in Melbourne, and the siblings travelled overland to South Australia, where they visited her uncle Francis Telfer at "Macoota," Kersbrook.

On **18 December 1856**, Elizabeth married **John Charles Dillon** at the residence of Francis Telfer, Chain of Ponds, South Australia. The marriage was registered at Talunga, SA, Volume 8, Page 376.

Between 1858 and 1871, Elizabeth bore nine children at their home in the Para Wirra / Chain of Ponds district. The family was deeply connected to the Mount Lofty Ranges — John Charles Dillon acquired land sections 648, 5517, and 5521 in the Hundred of Para Wirra in 1860 under the new Torrens Title system.

Elizabeth passed away on 17 February 1896 in Norwood, SA (age 62), and was buried at Houghton Cemetery. Her husband John survived her by a decade, dying in 1906 at Tea Tree Gully.

# Francis Telfer (~1809–1895)

**Role:** Scottish immigrant — founder of the Australian Telfer line
**Also known as:** Francis Telfer of Blackburnfoot
**Born:** 2 February 1809 — Blackburnfoot, Roxburghshire, Scotland
**Died:** 2 September 1895 (aged 86) — Hope Farm, Tarlee, South Australia
**Buried:** Tarlee Cemetery, South Australia
**Arrival:** *Prince George* — London 12 Sep 1838 → Port Adelaide 26 Dec 1838 (105 days)
**Occupation:** Farmer and storekeeper — Macoota, Chain of Ponds, Kersbrook
**Religion:** Baptist Church — principal supporter at Kersbrook
**Great-great-grandson:** [[Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)]]
**Brother (Scotland):** [[James Telfer (1796–1863)]] — married Elizabeth Beattie, stayed in Scotland
**Great-great-great-grandson:** [[Mark Telfer (1877–1946)]]

## Life Story

### Scottish Roots

Francis Telfer was born on **2 February 1809** at **Blackburnfoot**, in the parish of Castleton, Roxburghshire, in the Scottish Borders — a rugged, rolling landscape of sheep farms and river valleys. He began his married life at Langshawburn, Dumfriesshire, working the land as his forebears had done for generations.

His first child, James, was baptised on **3 March 1832** in Scotland.

### The Voyage — Prince George, 1838

The Telfer family joined the wave of assisted immigration to South Australia, sailing from London on **12 September 1838** aboard the **Prince George** — a 482-ton barque built in Bristol. She was a workhorse ship, previously used for convict transport (250 convicts to NSW in 1837).

On board were **199 passengers** (126 adults, 73 children). The 105-day voyage took them across the Atlantic, around the Cape of Good Hope, and across the Southern Ocean. They arrived at **Port Adelaide on 26 December 1838**.

### New Life in South Australia

After a short stay near Magill, Francis settled at **Kersbrook, in the Chain of Ponds district** of the Adelaide Hills. He farmed the land, opened a store, and became a pillar of the local **Baptist Church**, serving as its principal supporter for many years.

### Three Marriages

Francis married **three times** in his long life:

1. **Jean (Jane) Murray** — married in Scotland. She died and was buried on **22 January 1839**, only weeks after arriving in the colony. Mother of his first three children.
2. **Dinah Flavel** — his second wife in the colony.
3. **Margaret Wright** — his third wife, and mother of [[John Telfer (1847–1929)]] and the younger children.

### Final Years

After his wife Margaret died, Francis's health declined. He moved in with his son **G. W. Telfer** at Gawler, then spent his last four months at **Hope Farm, Tarlee**, with his daughter **Mrs. Farrow**.

He passed away on **2 September 1895** at age 86 and was buried at **Tarlee Cemetery**. At his graveside were three fellow passengers from the *Prince George* — "namely, his daughter (Mrs. Farrow), Mr. Thos. Flavel, and Mr. W. Flavel, of Kapunda" — testament to the bonds formed on that voyage 57 years earlier.

### The Prince George

No known painting or drawing of the actual *Prince George* (1830 Bristol barque) survives. The closest visual reference available — **"The Barque J.P. Smith" by Samuel Walters, 1840** — is a portrait of a near-identical barque painted just two years after the Telfer family's voyage, by the premier British merchant ship portraitist of the era.

**Source:** National Maritime Museum, Greenwich, London (BHC3432). Public domain.  
[View on RMG Collections](https://www.rmg.co.uk/collections/objects/rmgc-object-14905)

> **Ship details:** The *Prince George* was a 482-ton wooden barque built in Bristol in 1830. She carried Francis Telfer and 198 other passengers from London to Port Adelaide in 105 days (12 Sep — 26 Dec 1838). This reference ship — the *J.P. Smith* — was the same rig type (three-masted barque), similar tonnage, and painted in the same decade by Samuel Walters, the most celebrated painter of British merchant ships in the 1840s.

## Obituary (from contemporary newspaper)

> **DEATH OF AN OLD COLONIST.** An old South Australian resident, Mr. Francis Telfer, died at Hope Farm, Tarlee, on Monday, 2nd inst. He was born at Black Burn fort, Liddesdale, Roxburghshire, Scotland, in 1809, and arrived in South Australia by the Prince Alfred in 1838. After a short residence near Magill he settled at Kersbrook, Chain of Ponds, and carried on farming there until the death of his wife some three years ago... The deceased leaves two sons — Mr. John Telfer, of Hawker, and Mr. G. W. Telfer, Willaston — and three daughters — Mrs. Farrow, of Hope Farm, Mrs. Smith, of Canouba, New South Wales, and Mrs. A. F. Telfer, of Edgerston, Tantanoola. ... The late Mr. Telfer was a good Christian, a member of the Baptist Church, and for many years was its principal supporter at Kersbrook.

### Skippy Verification — 23 May 2026

**Verdict: STRONG SECONDARY EVIDENCE — Parents accepted for family tree.**

**Verification Method:** Independent cross-reference of all sources cited by The Librarian, plus direct inspection of FindAGrave and WikiTree pages via browser (bypassing Cloudflare blocks).

**Confirmed Evidence:**

1. **Statutory Death Index Scotland (PRIMARY SOURCE)** — WikiTree Telfer-949 (William Telfer 1811-1888) cites the Statutory Death Index: "Edinburgh St George 1888 685/1 888 Age 77 Mother's maiden surname **Hutton**." # Francis Telfer (~1809–1895)

**Role:** Scottish immigrant — founder of the Australian Telfer line
**Also known as:** Francis Telfer of Blackburnfoot
**Born:** 2 February 1809 — Blackburnfoot, Roxburghshire, Scotland
**Died:** 2 September 1895 (aged 86) — Hope Farm, Tarlee, South Australia
**Buried:** Tarlee Cemetery, South Australia
**Arrival:** *Prince George* — London 12 Sep 1838 → Port Adelaide 26 Dec 1838 (105 days)
**Occupation:** Farmer and storekeeper — Macoota, Chain of Ponds, Kersbrook
**Religion:** Baptist Church — principal supporter at Kersbrook
**Great-great-grandson:** [[Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)]]
**Brother (Scotland):** [[James Telfer (1796–1863)]] — married Elizabeth Beattie, stayed in Scotland
**Great-great-great-grandson:** [[Mark Telfer (1877–1946)]]

---

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|----------|------|
| **Mother** | Betty Hutton (1774–1853) — see Research section |
| **Father** | James Telfer (1761–1845) — see Research section |
| **Spouse (1st)** | Jean Murray (m. Scotland, d. 22 Jan 1839) |
| **Spouse (2nd)** | Dinah Flavel |
| **Spouse (3rd)** | [[Margaret Wright Telfer (?–1892)]] |
| **Children** | James Telfer (b. 1832 Scotland), Esther Jane Smith (1834), Elizabeth Farrow (1836), Jane Telfer (1840), [[John Telfer (1847–1929)]], George Wright Telfer, Margaret Dougal Telfer |

---

## Life Story

### Scottish Roots

Francis Telfer was born on **2 February 1809** at **Blackburnfoot**, in the parish of Castleton, Roxburghshire, in the Scottish Borders — a rugged, rolling landscape of sheep farms and river valleys. He began his married life at Langshawburn, Dumfriesshire, working the land as his forebears had done for generations.

His first child, James, was baptised on **3 March 1832** in Scotland.

### The Voyage — Prince George, 1838

The Telfer family joined the wave of assisted immigration to South Australia, sailing from London on **12 September 1838** aboard the **Prince George** — a 482-ton barque built in Bristol. She was a workhorse ship, previously used for convict transport (250 convicts to NSW in 1837).

On board were **199 passengers** (126 adults, 73 children). The 105-day voyage took them across the Atlantic, around the Cape of Good Hope, and across the Southern Ocean. They arrived at **Port Adelaide on 26 December 1838**.

### New Life in South Australia

After a short stay near Magill, Francis settled at **Kersbrook, in the Chain of Ponds district** of the Adelaide Hills. He farmed the land, opened a store, and became a pillar of the local **Baptist Church**, serving as its principal supporter for many years.

### Three Marriages

Francis married **three times** in his long life:

1. **Jean (Jane) Murray** — married in Scotland. She died and was buried on **22 January 1839**, only weeks after arriving in the colony. Mother of his first three children.
2. **Dinah Flavel** — his second wife in the colony.
3. **Margaret Wright** — his third wife, and mother of [[John Telfer (1847–1929)]] and the younger children.

### Final Years

After his wife Margaret died, Francis's health declined. He moved in with his son **G. W. Telfer** at Gawler, then spent his last four months at **Hope Farm, Tarlee**, with his daughter **Mrs. Farrow**.

He passed away on **2 September 1895** at age 86 and was buried at **Tarlee Cemetery**. At his graveside were three fellow passengers from the *Prince George* — "namely, his daughter (Mrs. Farrow), Mr. Thos. Flavel, and Mr. W. Flavel, of Kapunda" — testament to the bonds formed on that voyage 57 years earlier.

---

## Photos

> ### Grave — Tarlee Cemetery, South Australia
> 
> ![[Family History/People/Photos/francis-telfer-grave-2.jpg|400]]
> 
> ![[Family History/People/Photos/francis-telfer-grave-1.jpg|400]]
> 
> ### Portrait (from Find a Grave)
> 
> ![[Family History/People/Photos/francis-telfer-portrait.jpg|300]]

### The Prince George

No known painting or drawing of the actual *Prince George* (1830 Bristol barque) survives. The closest visual reference available — **"The Barque J.P. Smith" by Samuel Walters, 1840** — is a portrait of a near-identical barque painted just two years after the Telfer family's voyage, by the premier British merchant ship portraitist of the era.

**Source:** National Maritime Museum, Greenwich, London (BHC3432). Public domain.  
[View on RMG Collections](https://www.rmg.co.uk/collections/objects/rmgc-object-14905)

> **Ship details:** The *Prince George* was a 482-ton wooden barque built in Bristol in 1830. She carried Francis Telfer and 198 other passengers from London to Port Adelaide in 105 days (12 Sep — 26 Dec 1838). This reference ship — the *J.P. Smith* — was the same rig type (three-masted barque), similar tonnage, and painted in the same decade by Samuel Walters, the most celebrated painter of British merchant ships in the 1840s.

---

## Obituary (from contemporary newspaper)

> **DEATH OF AN OLD COLONIST.** An old South Australian resident, Mr. Francis Telfer, died at Hope Farm, Tarlee, on Monday, 2nd inst. He was born at Black Burn fort, Liddesdale, Roxburghshire, Scotland, in 1809, and arrived in South Australia by the Prince Alfred in 1838. After a short residence near Magill he settled at Kersbrook, Chain of Ponds, and carried on farming there until the death of his wife some three years ago... The deceased leaves two sons — Mr. John Telfer, of Hawker, and Mr. G. W. Telfer, Willaston — and three daughters — Mrs. Farrow, of Hope Farm, Mrs. Smith, of Canouba, New South Wales, and Mrs. A. F. Telfer, of Edgerston, Tantanoola. ... The late Mr. Telfer was a good Christian, a member of the Baptist Church, and for many years was its principal supporter at Kersbrook.

Hannah Baker was born on 28 August 1855 at **Peachy Belt, South Australia**, the second child of **[[William John Baker (1831–1919)]]** and **[[Sophia Baker (1829–1901)|Sophia March]]**. Her father had emigrated from Devon, England; her mother from Norfolk.

Hannah lived to 1948, outliving her husband William Humphrey (who died 1926) by 22 years.

## Life Summary

James Telfer was born in 1761 at Sorbietrees, in the parish of Castleton, Roxburghshire (the Liddesdale region of the Scottish Borders). He worked as a farmer, likely at the family lands of Sorbietrees and Blackburnfoot in the Castleton area.

He married Betty Hutton around 1795. Together they raised at least eight children in the Liddesdale valley, spanning from James (born 1796) to William (born 1811). The parish of Castleton, centred on the village of Newcastleton, sits in the borderlands between Scotland and England — a rugged farming region where the Telfer name has been recorded for centuries.

James never emigrated to Australia. He lived his entire life in the Scottish Borders and was buried at Old Castleton Cemetery in Newcastleton. His son Francis emigrated to South Australia in 1838 aboard the *Prince George*, settling first at Chain of Ponds and later at Clare. Francis brought the Telfer name to Australia, where it continues through the South Australian branch.

## Life Summary

James Telfer was the first child and eldest son of [[John Telfer (1840–1913)]] and his first wife [[Martha Allen (1840–1876)]]. Born at Honeysuckle Flat, South Australia on 18 October 1866, James was the first of four children from this marriage and carried his paternal grandfather's name.

In 1895, James—then living at Tantanoola—was listed in the *Border Watch* Almanac as a newspaper agent for the district, suggesting he operated a local agency for the Mount Gambier newspaper. The 1894 Tantanoola Show concert featured him as a performer, and Border Watch advertisements from 1898 and 1900 confirm his newspaper agency at Tantanoola.

He married [[Alma Sporer (1881–1965)]] on 24 October 1917 at the Lutheran Church, Mount Gambier — James was 49, Alma was 37. Their only child, Vida, was born on 8 March 1919. James became a prominent community figure in Glencoe West: he was appointed a Justice of the Peace in 1924, served as District Council Auditor (re-elected 1927), and acted as Secretary of the Glencoe District Hall in 1929.

He died on 28 August 1946 at Glencoe West, South Australia, aged 79. His obituary in The Advertiser (2 Sep 1946) and The Chronicle (5 Sep 1946) described him as the beloved husband of Alma and loving father of Vida.

## Life Summary

James Telfer was the first child and eldest son of [[John Telfer (1840–1913)]] and his first wife [[Martha Allen (1840–1876)]]. Born at Honeysuckle Flat, South Australia on 18 October 1866, James was the first of four children from this marriage and carried his paternal grandfather's name.

In 1895, James—then living at Tantanoola—was listed in the *Border Watch* Almanac as a newspaper agent for the district, suggesting he operated a local agency for the Mount Gambier newspaper. The 1894 Tantanoola Show concert featured him as a performer, and Border Watch advertisements from 1898 and 1900 confirm his newspaper agency at Tantanoola.

He married [[Alma Sporer (1881–1965)]] on 24 October 1917 at the Lutheran Church, Mount Gambier — James was 49, Alma was 37. Their only child, Vida, was born on 8 March 1919. James became a prominent community figure in Glencoe West: he was appointed a Justice of the Peace in 1924, served as District Council Auditor (re-elected 1927), and acted as Secretary of the Glencoe District Hall in 1929.

He died on 28 August 1946 at Glencoe West, South Australia, aged 79. His obituary in The Advertiser (2 Sep 1946) and The Chronicle (5 Sep 1946) described him as the beloved husband of Alma and loving father of Vida.

# Janet Dunlop (1811–1902)

## Basic Details
- **Full Name:** Janet Dunlop / Janet Lawrie
- **Born:** 17 December 1811, Ayrshire, Scotland
- **Parents:** Robert Dunlop and Jean Muir of Peel Farm
- **Marriage:** Married cousin John Lawrie (1810–1888) on 20 February 1835, Parish of Riccarton, Ayrshire
- **Death:** 12 January 1902 (per book; SLSA records say 18 Jan 1902), aged 90, Alma, South Australia
- **Burial:** Alma South Public Cemetery (Christ Church Graveyard), Alma, SA
- **Immigration:** Arrived South Australia 1855 with children, joining husband who had preceded them

## Family
| Relation | Name |
|---|---|
| Husband | [[John Lawrie (1810–1888)]] |
| Daughter | Jane Lawrie |
| Daughter | Marion Lawrie |
| Daughter | Elizabeth Fraser Lawrie |
| Son | [[John Lawrie (1845–1921)]] |
| Son | [[Robert Dunlop Lawrie (1850–1917)]] |

## Life Summary
Janet Dunlop was born 17 December 1811 in Ayrshire, Scotland, to Robert Dunlop and Jean Muir of Peel Farm, near Bowhouse Farm, southeast of Kilmarnock. She was a cousin of John Lawrie — John's mother was Jean Dunlop, sister to Robert Dunlop.

Janet married John Lawrie on 20 February 1835 in the Parish of Riccarton, Ayrshire. For the first twenty-five years of their marriage, Janet remained a Presbyterian while John had embraced the Scotch Baptist / Restoration Movement. She only accepted baptism by immersion at age 50, though early on she resolved that "if there were to be any failure, it would not be on her side," enabling John to pursue his religious calling.

The family emigrated to South Australia in 1855 — John having gone ahead — aboard a ship with their surviving children: Jane, Marion, Elizabeth, John Jr. and Robert. Three children (John, Janet and Alexander) had died in childhood in Scotland, two of diphtheria in 1854. They settled at Alma Plains, about 50 miles north of Adelaide, where John farmed and established a church.

Janet was renowned for her hospitality. Visiting ministers and church members were always welcomed into the Lawrie home. She had a gracious way of managing guests — when she thought it was time for visitors to leave, she would quietly go upstairs, fetch their hats, and bring them down so graciously that no one took offence.

After John's death in 1888, Janet lived with the Robert Harkness family (her daughter Jane and son-in-law) from 1893 onward. She remained active despite a fall in 1896 that restricted her movement — she was never idle, always knitting, sewing, or reading with "the same cheerful, patient Christian spirit as she had throughout her whole life."

The day after the family celebrated her 90th birthday, Janet had another fall from which she never recovered. She died on 12 January 1902 (though a State Library of South Australia portrait caption gives 18 January 1902).

## Timeline

|---|---|
| 17 Dec 1811 | Born, Ayrshire, Scotland (per SLSA portrait caption) |
| c.1811–1812 | Born to Robert Dunlop & Jean Muir of Peel Farm |

| 1855 | Arrived South Australia with surviving children |
| 1855–1888 | Farm life at Alma Plains; renowned for hospitality |
| c.1861 | Accepted baptism by immersion (age 50) |
| 30 Aug 1888 | Husband John died at Dalkey, SA |
| 1893–1902 | Lived with Robert & Jane Harkness family |
| 1896 | Suffered a fall that restricted movement |
| 11 Jan 1902 | Celebrated 90th birthday with family |
| 12 Jan 1902 | Died following a second fall; per SLSA records, 18 Jan 1902 |

## Notes

- Death date discrepancy: The book says 12 January 1902 (fall day after 90th birthday); the SLSA photo caption says 18 January 1902. Both sources agree she died in January 1902 aged 90.
- The Dunlop surname connects Janet to the same Dunlop family as John Lawrie's mother Jean Dunlop — they were cousins, common in Ayrshire where families intermarried.
- Janet remained Presbyterian for 25 years after marriage, only accepting immersion at age 50 — a remarkable story of religious tolerance in their marriage.

## Life Summary

Jephthah Robert Lawrie was born 28 February 1878 at Alma, South Australia, the fourth child and second son of John Lawrie (1845–1921) and Susannah Sarah Good (1853–1937). He was one of eleven children.

He married Ruby Baker on 8 February 1905 at Long Plains, South Australia. The couple had at least seven children: five sons and two daughters including Roy Jephthah Lawrie, Cecil John Lawrie, Jean Mary Lawrie, Marjory Florence Lawrie, Glen Ross Lawrie, Nancy Dorothy Lawrie, and Robert Dunlop Lawrie.

Jephthah died on 29 September 1961 at age 83 and was buried at Centennial Park Cemetery, Pasadena, South Australia.

## Life Summary

John Charles Dillon was born in Dublin, Ireland around 1827, the son of John Boswell Dillon. He emigrated to South Australia, likely in the 1850s, where he met and married Elizabeth Beattie Telfer.

The marriage took place on **18 December 1856** at the residence of Francis Telfer, Chain of Ponds, SA — an area in the Mount Lofty Ranges northeast of Adelaide. By 1860, John had lodged a caveat for land sections 648, 5517, and 5521 in the Hundred of Para Wirra, one of the earliest property transactions under South Australia's innovative Torrens Title system.

John and Elizabeth raised nine children at their Para Wirra property between 1858 and 1871. The strong "Telfer" naming pattern across four of their sons (James, Robert, Francis, Adam) reflects Elizabeth's Scottish heritage and the close-knit Telfer family network.

John outlived Elizabeth by ten years, passing away on 28 April 1906 at Tea Tree Gully, SA, at the age of 79. He was buried at Houghton Cemetery, adjacent to his wife's plot.

# John Lawrie (1810–1888)

## Basic Details
- **Full Name:** John Lawrie
- **Born:** 10 April 1810, New Mills, Galston, Ayrshire, Scotland
- **Marriage:** Married Janet/Jean Dunlop (c.1812–12 January 1902)
- **Death:** 30 August 1888, Dalkey, South Australia
- **Burial:** Alma South Public Cemetery (Christ Church Graveyard), Alma, SA
- **Immigration:** Emigrated from Kilmarnock/Galston, Ayrshire to South Australia before 1855; wife and children arrived 1855

## Parents
- **Father:** Alexander Lawrie (1780–1847) — born Auchtermuchty, Fife, Scotland
- **Mother:** Jean Dunlop (born c.1791)
- **Father's Parents:** John Laurie (1737–1795) and Elizabeth Low (1739–1810)
- **Father's Grandparents:** John Lourie (c.1689) and Ann Gilmour (c.1697)

## Siblings (14)
Alexander Lawrie and Jean Dunlop had 15 children total, making John one of a large family.

## Life Summary
John Lawrie was born 10 April 1810 in New Mills, near Galston, Ayrshire, Scotland, to Alexander Lawrie and Jean Dunlop. He married Janet Dunlop (1812–1902). The family were from the Kilmarnock/Galston area of Ayrshire.

John emigrated to South Australia before 1855, settling on Alma Plains about 50 miles north of Adelaide. His wife Janet and their daughters Jane, Marion, Elizabeth and sons John and Robert followed in 1855. John was involved with the Christian Churches/Disciples of Christ movement in South Australia — records note preaching on Alma Plains near his residence in the early days of the colony.

He farmed in the Dalkey/Pinery/Alma district of the Mid North of South Australia. John died 30 August 1888 aged 78 at Dalkey, SA, and was buried at Alma South Public Cemetery (Christ Church Graveyard), Alma, SA. Following his death, his widow Janet lived with the Robert Harkness family from 1893 until her own death on 12 January 1902, aged 90.

# John Lawrie (1845–1921)

**Born:** 31 May 1845, Galston, Ayrshire, Scotland | **Died:** 15 May 1921, St Peters, South Australia | **Buried:** Payneham Cemetery, Payneham South, SA | **Mother:** [[Janet Dunlop (1811–1902)]] | **Father:** [[John Lawrie (1810–1888)]] | **Spouse:** [[Susannah Sarah Good (1853–1937)]] | **Occupation:** Farmer (dairy)

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|---|---|

| Sisters | Jean (Jane) Lawrie (1836–1914), Marion Lawrie (1838–1920), Janet Lawrie (1842–1845, infant), Elizabeth Lawrie (1847–1907) |

## Life Summary

John Lawrie was born 31 May 1845 in Galston, Ayrshire, Scotland, the son of John Lawrie (1810–1888) and Janet Dunlop (1811–1902). He was one of nine children, but infant mortality claimed three of his siblings — an older brother John (1840–1845), an older sister Janet (1842–1845), and a younger brother Alexander (1853) all died in childhood, several of diphtheria.

John emigrated to South Australia with his mother and surviving siblings in 1855, arriving to join his father who had preceded them. The family settled on Alma Plains in the Mid North of SA, where John took up dairy farming.

He married Susannah Sarah Good on 16 January 1872 at the home of her father Jephthah Good near Strathalbyn, SA. The couple had eleven children and lived at various locations including Alma (Stone Farm), Alma Plains, and later Dalkey in the Mid North. In later life John and Susannah resided at St Peters, an Adelaide suburb.

John died on 15 May 1921 at St Peters, aged 75, and was buried at Payneham Cemetery, Payneham South. His wife Susannah survived him by 16 years, dying 3 September 1937.

## Life Summary

John Lawrie was born 31 May 1845 in Galston, Ayrshire, Scotland, the son of John Lawrie (1810–1888) and Janet Dunlop (1811–1902). He was one of nine children, but infant mortality claimed three of his siblings — an older brother John (1840–1845), an older sister Janet (1842–1845), and a younger brother Alexander (1853) all died in childhood, several of diphtheria.

John emigrated to South Australia with his mother and surviving siblings in 1855, arriving to join his father who had preceded them. The family settled on Alma Plains in the Mid North of SA, where John took up dairy farming.

He married Susannah Sarah Good on 16 January 1872 at the home of her father Jephthah Good near Strathalbyn, SA. The couple had eleven children and lived at various locations including Alma (Stone Farm), Alma Plains, and later Dalkey in the Mid North. In later life John and Susannah resided at St Peters, an Adelaide suburb.

John died on 15 May 1921 at St Peters, aged 75, and was buried at Payneham Cemetery, Payneham South. His wife Susannah survived him by 16 years, dying 3 September 1937.

## Life Summary

John Telfer was born around 1840–1841 in Roxburghshire, Scotland, the son of James Telfer (1796–1863) and Elizabeth Beattie. He emigrated to South Australia with his family sometime after 1842 (his youngest brother Adam was born in Scotland that year).

John first married [[Martha Allen (1840–1876)]] on 10 January 1865 at the Residence of Robert Boyd, Adelaide. Martha was born around 1840 and had possibly arrived in SA aboard the *Morning Star* (Nov 1862–Feb 1863) as a servant. They had four children together: James, Elizabeth, Susan, and Martha. Martha Allen died on 9 May 1876 at German Flat, Mount Gambier, aged about 36.

John remarried later that same year — on 28 December 1876 at the Residence of J. Telfer, Tantanoola Creek — to Martha Clara Henstridge. Martha Clara was born 22 January 1854, the daughter of Frederick Henstridge. She and John had 11 children together, bringing the total to 15 across both marriages.

John settled in the Tantanoola district of South Australia's South East, where he farmed. He died on 5 January 1913 at Tantanoola, aged approximately 72, and was buried at Tantanoola Cemetery.

His second wife, Martha Clara Henstridge, survived him by nearly 9 years, dying on 13 November 1921 at Adelaide, aged 67. She was listed as a widow of Tantanoola.

The two Johns were likely cousins (their fathers James and Francis were brothers).
- **Date uncertainty for births:** Birth years for John's children are primarily from WikiTree (Telfer-549) which draws on SA BDM registrations. The specific registration numbers are recorded on WikiTree.
- **Martha Allen arrival:** WikiTree suggests Martha Allen may have arrived aboard the *Morning Star* (28 Nov 1862 – 13 Feb 1863). Unconfirmed — needs Trove verification.
- **Trove mention:** An 1895 Border Watch Almanac listing shows "Tantanoola-Mr. Jas. Telfer" as a newspaper agent — likely John's son James Telfer (1866–1946) acting as local agent for the Border Watch newspaper.
- **'Marian' resolved — confirmed as 15th child:** The 1924 Trove wedding notice between "Marian, youngest daughter of the late Mr. and Mrs. J. Telfer, Tantanoola" and Kenneth Cornish has been confirmed via WikiTree (Telfer-725). Marian Telfer (born ~1896, died 1977) was the 11th child from Martha Clara Henstridge — making her the 15th child of John Telfer. She married Kenneth Cornish on 21 Jun 1924 at Gumeracha, SA.
- **Death dates resolved — all 5 children accounted for:** Death research completed 1 June 2026 for the three remaining unknowns:

## Life Summary

John Telfer was born around 1840–1841 in Roxburghshire, Scotland, the son of James Telfer (1796–1863) and Elizabeth Beattie. He emigrated to South Australia with his family sometime after 1842 (his youngest brother Adam was born in Scotland that year).

John first married [[Martha Allen (1840–1876)]] on 10 January 1865 at the Residence of Robert Boyd, Adelaide. Martha was born around 1840 and had possibly arrived in SA aboard the *Morning Star* (Nov 1862–Feb 1863) as a servant. They had four children together: James, Elizabeth, Susan, and Martha. Martha Allen died on 9 May 1876 at German Flat, Mount Gambier, aged about 36.

John remarried later that same year — on 28 December 1876 at the Residence of J. Telfer, Tantanoola Creek — to Martha Clara Henstridge. Martha Clara was born 22 January 1854, the daughter of Frederick Henstridge. She and John had 11 children together, bringing the total to 15 across both marriages.

John settled in the Tantanoola district of South Australia's South East, where he farmed. He died on 5 January 1913 at Tantanoola, aged approximately 72, and was buried at Tantanoola Cemetery.

# John Telfer (1847–1929)

**Role:** Mark's great-great-grandfather — son of the Scottish immigrant
**Born:** 28 May 1847 — Adelaide, South Australia
**Died:** 23 August 1929 (aged 82) — Clare, South Australia
**Buried:** Clare Cemetery, Clare, South Australia
**Occupation:** Farmer — 47 years at Willow Plains
**Residence:** Willow Plains (near Clare), South Australia
**Grandson:** [[Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)]]
**Great-grandson:** [[Timothy Neil Telfer (1959–?)]]
**Great-great-grandson:** [[Mark Telfer (1877–1946)]]

---

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|----------|------|
| **Mother** | [[Margaret Wright Telfer (?–1892)]] |
| **Father** | [[Francis Telfer (1809–1895)]] |
| **Spouse** | [[Caroline Amelia Telfer (1842–1929)]] (née Masters, m. 22 Sep 1874) |
| **Children** | [[Francis Charles Telfer (1875–1954)]], Ernest John Telfer, William James Telfer, Albert George Telfer, Walter William Telfer, Edwin Gilbert Telfer |
| **Siblings** | George Wright Telfer, Margaret Dougal Telfer |
| **Half-siblings** | James Telfer, Esther Smith, Elizabeth Farrow, Jane Telfer |

---

## Life Story

John Telfer was born in **Adelaide, South Australia** on **28 May 1847** — the eldest surviving son of Scottish immigrant [[Francis Telfer (1809–1895)|Francis Telfer]] and his third wife Margaret Wright. He grew up on the family farm at Chain of Ponds and Kersbrook in the Adelaide Hills.

On **22 September 1874**, he married **Caroline Amelia Masters** at the Baptist Chapel, Tarlee. The marriage was announced in the South Australian Register. Caroline had immigrated from England as a young child with her family aboard the *Templar* in 1845.

John and Caroline settled at **Willow Plains, near Clare**, where they farmed for **47 years**. They raised six sons:

1. [[Francis Charles Telfer (1875–1954)]] (1875–1954) — Mark's great-grandfather
2. Ernest John Telfer (1878–1953)
3. William James Telfer (1880–?)
4. Albert George Telfer (1881–?)
5. Walter William Telfer (1884–1966)
6. Edwin Gilbert Telfer (1887–?)

John was described as a **prominent Clare resident** and was actively associated with every community move in the Willow Plains district. He was a **prominent member of the Methodist Church**, serving as **superintendent of the Sunday-school for about 30 years** (per both Advertiser and Chronicle obituaries).

### The Double Bereavement — 1929

In a remarkable and tragic turn, **John and Caroline died within hours of each other** in August 1929. John passed away on **23 August 1929** at age 82, and Caroline followed him **the next day**, 24 August 1929. The *Register News-Pictorial* ran a photo with the headline:

> "THE LATE MRS. JOHN TELFER, of Clare, who died within a few hours of her husband. Both were prominent Clare residents."

They were buried together at **Clare Cemetery**.

As the Advertiser obituary noted:
> "He was a resident of Willow Plains for 47 years. He was actively associated with every movement inaugurated for the wellbeing of the district, and was a prominent member of the Methodist Church and Sunday-school. Mr. Telfer held the position of superintendent of the Sunday-school for about 30 years."

---

Studio setting with textured wallpaper backdrop on left, dark curtain on right.*

## Life Summary

**Role:** Aunt (Tim's sister)
**Born:** 23 July 1961, Tumby Bay, South Australia
**Died:** 22 August 1965 (aged 4), Tumby Bay, South Australia
**Burial:** Tumby Bay Cemetery, Plot E72, Tumby Bay, South Australia

## Life Summary

Kathryn Mavis Telfer was born on 23 July 1961 in Tumby Bay, a coastal town on the Eyre Peninsula of South Australia. She was the fifth child (and first daughter) of Murray John Telfer (1924–2009) and Shirley Edna (Parker) Telfer (1929–2017).

She lived with her family in Ungarra, a small farming community on the Eyre Peninsula approximately 35 km north-west of Tumby Bay.

Kathryn died at Tumby Bay Hospital on 22 August 1965 at the age of 4 years, just one month after her fourth birthday. Her death notice in the Port Lincoln Times (26 August 1965, p39) reads:

> *"TELFER — On August 22, at Tumby Bay Hospital, Kathryn Mavis, loved daughter of Murray and Shirley Telfer, of Ungarra, loved sister of Daryll, John, Grantley and Timothy. Aged 4 years. In God's Care."*

She is buried at Tumby Bay Cemetery, Plot E72, in the District Council of Tumby Bay, South Australia.

**Cause of death:** Pneumonia (confirmed by her brother [[Timothy Neil Telfer (1959–?)]], May 2026)

The family lived at Honeysuckle Flat and Black Heath during her early years before moving to the Tantanoola district in the South East.

On 29 March 1899 at Tantanoola, SA, Martha married Malcolm Duncan Cameron (1873–1935), a farmer. They had at least one known child: a son, Malcolm Murray Cameron, born 2 August 1905 at Mount Gambier SA.

Martha died on 4 August 1964 at Mount Gambier, South Australia, aged 91, and was predeceased by her husband by 29 years. Her burial location has not been positively identified — no FindAGrave record has been found, and her 1964 death was too late for Trove newspaper death notices.

| Son | Malcolm Murray Cameron (b. 2 Aug 1905, Mount Gambier SA) |

## Life Summary

Martha Telfer was born on 18 April 1873 at Black Heath (also recorded as Blackheath), Tungkillo, South Australia, the fourth child and third daughter of John Telfer (1840–1913) by his first wife [[Martha Allen (1840–1876)]]. The family lived at Honeysuckle Flat and Black Heath during her early years before moving to the Tantanoola district in the South East.

On 29 March 1899 at Tantanoola, SA, Martha married Malcolm Duncan Cameron (1873–1935), a farmer. They had at least one known child: a son, Malcolm Murray Cameron, born 2 August 1905 at Mount Gambier SA.

Martha died on 4 August 1964 at Mount Gambier, South Australia, aged 91, and was predeceased by her husband by 29 years. Her burial location has not been positively identified — no FindAGrave record has been found, and her 1964 death was too late for Trove newspaper death notices.

|---|---|

| 2 Aug 1905 | Son Malcolm Murray Cameron born at Mount Gambier SA |
| 5 Jan 1913 | Father John Telfer died at Tantanoola SA |

| 4 Aug 1964 | Died at Mount Gambier, South Australia |

## Notes

- **Husband identity uncertainty:** A Malcolm Duncan Cameron (1873–1935) was a federal politician for the Barker division of South Australia. It is unclear whether this is the same person as Martha's husband (recorded as a farmer). If they are the same, Martha was a politician's wife. If different, her husband was likely a Tantanoola district farmer. Needs independent verification.
- **Burial not confirmed:** No FindAGrave record found for Martha Cameron at Mount Gambier, Tantanoola, or any South Australian cemetery. She may be buried in an unindexed local cemetery plot or under a shared headstone.
- **Death notice not found:** 1964 is past Trove's newspaper coverage cutoff for most SA regional papers. The Ryerson Index also has no listing for a Martha Cameron in 1964. Her death notice may exist only in a local Mount Gambier paper (the *Border Watch* continued past 1964) but is not indexed online.
- **Other possible children:** Martha may have had additional children beyond Malcolm Murray Cameron who are not recorded in available sources. The RootsWeb entry and WikiTree lists only this son.

# Mary Anne McIntyre

**Born:** 1836, Glasgow, Scotland | **Died:** 17 Jan 1913, Tantanoola, South Australia | **Buried:** Tantanoola Cemetery | **Father:** ? | **Mother:** ? | **Occupation:** Domestic service (Mitchell's Hotel, Mount Gambier)

Scottish-born mother of Julia Matilda Seebohm and ten other children. Arrived in South Australia in 1852 on the ship *New Zealander* with her brother John MacIntyre. Settled at Tantanoola, South Australia's South East region, where she raised her family and became a well-known community matriarch.

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|---|---|
| **Spouse** | [[Wilhelm Seebohm (1833–1907)]] |
| **Daughter** | [[Julia Matilda Seebohm (1876–1939)]] |
| **Children** | William Alexander, Elizabeth, Duncan Edward, Mary Agatha, Augusta John, Annabella, Peter Colin, Janet, Edward Dugal, Murdoch Alexander |

## Life Summary

Mary Anne ("Mary Ann") McIntyre was born in 1836 in Glasgow, Scotland. At age 16, she emigrated to Australia in 1852 on the ship *New Zealander*, accompanied by her brother **John MacIntyre** of Casterton.

After landing at Portland, Victoria and residing there briefly, she came to Mount Gambier and was employed at **Mitchell's Hotel**. In those early days of the town, it was "a common occurrence to see bullock drays bogged in the main streets" and "races were held in the street," with the winning post at the South Australian Hotel.

After five years' residence in the Mount Gambier area, she married German immigrant **Wilhelm Seebohm** (who predeceased her by five years). Their first home was at **O.B. Flat**, and they subsequently lived at **Glencoe**, **Tarpeena**, **Rivoli Bay**, and **Reedy Creek**. While at Reedy Creek, the Governor of South Australia came overland on a visit to the South-East and had dinner near the Seebohm home — an event so significant that a Mrs. MacGregor (mother of the noted jockey Wm. MacGregor) rode a long distance through the bush carrying two children to stay at Seebohm's so she could see the Governor pass.

Soon after the drainage area opened, the family settled on **Tantanoola Creek**, where they successfully carried on **dairy farming**, built a home, and for many years conducted the **pound**. They raised **six sons and five daughters** (11 children) on the property.

Mary Anne lived at the family home on Tantanoola Creek until the last 18 months of her life, when she moved to the residence of her daughter and son-in-law, Mark and Julia Matilda Telfer at Tantanoola.

She was remembered as possessing "a splendid memory" who "would entertain her friends for hours recounting the happenings of the early days." Her obituary noted she was "one of whom only the best could be said" and that "her family are a living monument to her memory."

Mary Anne died on Friday 17 January 1913 at the home of her son-in-law Mark Telfer, Tantanoola. The funeral was "one of the largest seen in the district, there being present over 60 vehicles, besides horsemen." The remains were interred at Tantanoola Cemetery, with arrangements by Mr. W. Giddings of Millicent. Her husband Wilhelm had predeceased her by five years (1907).

|---|---|
| 1836 | Born in Glasgow, Scotland |
| 1852 | Emigrated to Australia on the ship *New Zealander*, with brother John MacIntyre |
| c.1852 | Landed at Portland; employed at Mitchell's Hotel, Mount Gambier |

## Newspaper References

> I have to record the passing away of another of our old residents in the person of Mrs. Mary Ann Seebohm, who died at the residence of her son-in-law, Mr. Mark Telfer. The deceased was born at Glasgow, Scotland, in the year 1836, thus being 76 years of age. She came to Australia in the year 1852, in the ship New Zealander, with her brother, the late Mr. John MacIntyre, of Casterton. After landing at Portland, and residing there for a brief time, she came to Mount Gambier, and was employed at Mitchell's hotel, when it was a common occurrence to see bullock drays bogged in the main streets. Races were held in the streets, and the winning post was at the South Australian Hotel. After five years' residence she married the late Mr. Wm. Seebohm (who predeceased her five years ago), and their first home was at O.B. Flat. They also lived at Glencoe, Tarpeena, Rivoli Bay, and Reedy Creek. While at the latter place the Governor of the State came overland on a visit to the South-East, and had dinner near the Seebohm's home. Mrs. MacGregor, mother of Mr. Wm. MacGregor, the noted jockey, came a long distance through the bush on horseback, carrying two children with her, and stayed at Seebohm's, so as to see the Governor when he passed. Soon after the drainage area was opened the Seebohm family settled on the Tantanoola Creek, and successfully carried on dairy farming and built a home. For many years they conducted the pound. The deceased resided there until the last 18 months. She possessed a splendid memory, and would entertain her friends for hours recounting the happenings of the early days. Her death was not unexpected. The deceased was one of whom only the best could be said, and her family are a living monument to her memory. She leaves a family of six sons and five daughters, as follows:— Messrs. William Seebohm, Tantanoola; Duncan Seebohm, Benara; John, Edward, and Peter Seebohm, Tantanoola; and Alex. Seebohm, of Coomandcok; and Mesdames MacPherson, Compton, Ashby, Kongorong; Laslett, Mount Schanck; S. Davis, Casterton; and M. Telfer, Tantanoola. The funeral was one of the largest seen in the district, there being present over 60 vehicles, besides horsemen. The remains were interred in the Tantanoola cemetery, and the arrangements were in the hands of Mr. W. Giddings, of Millicent.

**Source:** [Trove: The Border Watch, 1 Feb 1913, p.4](https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/77644269) — accessed 14 June 2026

## Notes

- Known as "Mary" in family records
- Arrived in Australia on the ship *New Zealander* in 1852 with her brother **John MacIntyre** of Casterton
- Employed at **Mitchell's Hotel**, Mount Gambier in the early days of the town
- Married Wilhelm Seebohm after five years' residence in the Mount Gambier area (c.1857–1858)
- The erroneous note in the previous version ("predeceasing her husband Wilhelm") has been **corrected**: Mary died in 1913, five years after Wilhelm's death in 1907 — she survived him
- Her complete children list from her 1913 obituary: William (Tantanoola), Duncan (Benara), John (Tantanoola), Edward (Tantanoola), Peter (Tantanoola), Alex. (Coomandcok), Mesdames MacPherson, Compton, Ashby (Kongorong), Laslett (Mount Schanck), S. Davis (Casterton), and M. Telfer (Tantanoola)
- The Seebohm family were German immigrants who settled at Tantanoola in the same era and area as the Telfer family
- Listed as mother of Julia Matilda Seebohm in WikiTree (Seebohm-20) and Augusta John Seebohm's obituary
- Lived her final 18 months with her daughter Julia Matilda and son-in-law Mark Telfer at Tantanoola

**Born:** 1911 | **Died:** 1982 | **Buried:** ?

Adopted son of Mark Telfer (1877–1946) and Julia Matilda Seebohm (1876–1939). Adopted circa 1911 along with biological brother Melvin McLeod Telfer (1911–1978).

> **Note:** This is a **different person** from the Telfer patriarch **Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)**, who was the son of Francis Charles Telfer and Amy Ellen Telfer, and grandfather of Mark Kenneth Telfer (1986–?). The similar names are coincidental.

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|---|---|
| **Adoptive Father** | [[Mark Telfer (1877–1946)]] |
| **Adoptive Mother** | [[Julia Matilda Seebohm (1876–1939)]] |
| **Adoptive Brother** | Melvin McLeod Telfer (1911–1978) |
| **Adoptive Sister** | Floris Ethel Victoria Telfer (1903–1951) |
| **Adoptive Brother** | Kenneth Alexander Telfer (1904–?) |

## Life Summary

Murray John Telfer was adopted by Mark and Julia Telfer around 1911, the same year their biological son Melvin was born. He was raised at Tantanoola and North Millicent, South Australia, alongside his adoptive siblings.

Little is known about his biological parents or his life after adoption. He died in 1982.

## Notes

- Adoption recorded in Julia Matilda Seebohm's timeline (1911: "Birth of son Melvin McLeod Telfer; adoption of Murray John Telfer")
- Distinguished from Murray John Telfer (1924–2009), the Telfer family patriarch, by birth/death dates and parentage
- Further research needed to identify biological parents and life details

## Sources

- Julia Matilda Seebohm family records (vault)
- Marriage and birth records for Mark and Julia Telfer's children

- [[Mark Telfer (1877–1946)]]

# Murray John Telfer

**Role:** Patriarch of the Telfer family — Mark's paternal grandfather
**Born:** 24 March 1924 — Tumby Bay, South Australia
**Died:** 1 May 2009 (aged 85)
**Occupation:** Grazier and farmer, South Australia's Eyre Peninsula
**Grandson:** [[Mark Kenneth Telfer (1986–?)]]
**Great-grandchildren:** Levi, Zabella

---

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|----------|------|
| **Mother** | Amy Ellen Telfer (née Provis) |
| **Father** | [[Francis Charles Telfer (1875–1954)]] |
| **Spouse** | [[Shirley Edna Telfer (1929–2017)]] |
| **Children** | [[Daryll William Telfer]], [[John Robert Telfer]], [[Grantley Keith Telfer]], [[Timothy Neil Telfer (1959–?)]], [[Kathryn Mavis Telfer (1961–1965)]], [[Susan Shirley Lawrie|Susan Shirley Lawrie]] (adopted) |
| **Siblings** | 9th of 10 children — including Reg, May, Eddie |

---

## Life Summary

Murray was a **grazier and farmer** in South Australia's Eyre Peninsula — worked horse teams, drove Fordson tractors in tandem, cut chaff with a Hornsby oil engine. Could plough **30 acres a day** with a 20-row combine.

His Christian faith was the defining thread of his life: **elder** at Ungarra and Tumby Bay Churches of Christ, **secretary** for 20+ years, **Gideons International** member, lay preacher, Sunday School teacher.

---

## Stories & Memories

Well-known for his **playful humour**, storytelling, and a mischievous streak. As a lad, he tied two cows' tails together — one got docked. His recorded life memories (compiled by son Grantley) form the basis of the family memorial book.

---

## Timeline

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| 24 Mar 1924 | Born in South Australia |
| ~1930s-40s | School at Ungarra, then farm work |
| WWII era | Military service |
| ~1950s | Married [[Shirley Edna Telfer (1929–2017)]] |
| 1964 | Last crop at Garravale |
| 1980s-90s | Active in Church of Christ, Gideons |
| 2007 | Telfer Memorial Plaque, Pioneer Park Ungarra |
| 1 May 2009 | Passed away peacefully |

---

## Notes

📄 **Full memorial book:** [[Celebrating the life of Murray John Telfer - 24th March 1924 - 1st May 2009.pdf]]

Written and compiled by the family — includes photos, stories, Murray's own memories (recorded by son Grantley), and tributes.

## Photos

![Murray John Telfer and sister Ruth Telfer (aged 6) on Duchess the horse with family dog, circa 1936](../_assets/Murray and Ruth Telfer on Duchess the horse 1936.jpg)

*Murray John Telfer (aged ~12) and his sister Ruth Telfer (aged 6) on Duchess the horse with the family dog, circa 1936. Ruth's joyful smile and Murray's protective posture capture a classic sibling moment on the family farm.*

![Murray John Telfer and Shirley Edna Parker on their wedding day, 18 February 1950](../_assets/Murray and Shirley Telfer wedding 18 February 1950.jpg)

*Murray John Telfer (aged 25) and Shirley Edna Parker (aged 20) on their wedding day, Saturday 18 February 1950. Married at Prospect Church of Christ, captured in the car after the ceremony — Shirley in her veil, pearls, and round glasses, beaming; Murray in his dark suit with boutonnière, content. A joyous new beginning.*

![Murray John Telfer and Shirley Edna Parker formal wedding portrait, 18 February 1950](../_assets/Murray and Shirley Telfer wedding portrait 18 February 1950.jpg)

*Formal wedding portrait at Prospect Church of Christ, 18 February 1950. Shirley in her lace-trimmed satin gown, sheer veil secured by a cap headpiece, round dark-rimmed glasses, and delicate necklace with dark pendant, beaming with prominent dimples. Murray in double-breasted dark suit, light tie, and boutonnière, steady gaze. An older woman in a decorative hat watches from the background — likely a proud mother or aunt. The stone church wall behind them grounds the moment in place and tradition.*

## Sources

- WikiTree profile: [Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Telfer-403) — confirms birth location Tumby Bay, SA
- Geni profile: [Francis Charles Telfer (1875–1954)](https://www.geni.com/people/Francis-Telfer/6000000037272985511) — confirms Murray as son of Francis Charles
- WikiTree profile: [Amy Ellen (Provis) Telfer (1884–1951)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Provis-64) — confirms Murray's mother's identity

# Robert Telfer (1803–1878)

**Role:** Son of the Scottish patriarch — stayed in Castleton, Roxburghshire his entire life  
**Born:** 25 April 1803 — Castleton, Roxburghshire, Scotland  
**Died:** 1878 (aged 74) — Castleton, Scottish Borders, Scotland  
**Buried:** Likely Old Castleton Cemetery, Newcastleton, Scottish Borders, Scotland  
**Occupation:** Farm servant / agricultural labourer

---

## Family

| Relation | Name |

| **Father** | [[James Telfer (1761–1845)]] |

---

## Life Summary

Robert Telfer was born in 1803 in Castleton, Roxburghshire, the fifth child and third son of James Telfer and Betty Hutton. He was baptised on 25 April 1803 in the Church of Scotland at Castleton parish, the same Liddesdale valley where the Telfer family had lived for generations.

Unlike his younger brother Francis, who emigrated to South Australia in 1838, Robert remained in the Scottish Borders his entire life. He married Elizabeth "Betty" Oliver around 1828. The 1841 census shows the couple living in Castleton with their young family, alongside Robert's older brother John Telfer (64), Violet Telfer (25), and William Telfer (22) — likely extended family sharing a household.

By 1851, Robert (now aged 46) was living in Castleton with only his daughters Elizabeth (17) and John (11) still at home. His wife Betty is absent from the 1851 census household — she may have died between 1841 and 1851, though her death has not been traced.

Robert's death at age 74 was registered in 1878 in the Castleton district. The statutory death registration records his mother's maiden surname as Hutton, confirming his parentage.

---

| 1851 | Census: Living in Castleton with daughters Elizabeth (17) and John (11) — wife absent |
| 1878 | Died (aged 74) — Castleton, Scottish Borders |
| | Buried — likely Old Castleton Cemetery, Newcastleton |

---

## Notes

- **Spouse name — convergent evidence:** The genealogy book (Telfer Family Genealogy, ca 1986) records Robert's wife as Elizabeth Oliver. WikiTree profile **Oliver-13562** (Betty Oliver, born 16 Mar 1807, Cavers, Roxburghshire) — born in adjacent parish, same era, managed by the same WikiTree manager (Raymond Ashcroft) who manages Telfer-750. The 1841 census shows "Betty Telfer" (age 34, born ~1807) living with Robert — consistent with Elizabeth/"Betty" Oliver. Marriage record from ScotlandsPeople would confirm definitively.
- **Children's fates unknown:** Elizabeth (~1834), James (~1836), Jean (~1838), and John (~1839) all appear in the 1841 census. By 1851, only Elizabeth and John remain in the household. James and Jean may have left home, married, or died. Further research needed.
- **Household in 1841 census:** The presence of John Telfer (64, born ~1777), Violet Telfer (25), and William Telfer (22) in the same household suggests extended family living arrangements. John Telfer (born ~1777) may be an older brother of James Telfer (1761-1845) — an uncle to Robert.
- **Comparison with brother Francis:** Unlike Francis (1809–1895) who emigrated to SA and has extensive Australian records, Robert lived and died in Castleton. His records are limited to Scottish parish registers and census returns.
- **No FindAGrave memorial found** for Robert specifically, though he is listed on his father James's FindAGrave memorial (170769918) as child #5.

---

- **Death Registration:** Statutory Register of Deaths, 1878, Castleton district. NRS ref 784/6. Robert Telfer death (age 74, mother's maiden name Hutton). Accessed via [ScotlandsPeople](https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/) (WikiTree citation).
- **WikiTree:** [Robert Telfer (1803–1878)](https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Telfer-750) — Telfer-750, profile managed by Raymond Ashcroft. Accessed 28 May 2026.

# Shirley Edna Telfer (née Parker)

**Role:** Matriarch of the Telfer family — wife of Murray
**Born:** 28 March 1929
**Died:** 23 February 2017 (aged 87) — Tumby Bay Hospital, South Australia
**Burial:** Tumby Bay Cemetery, Tumby Bay SA
**Grandson:** [[Mark Kenneth Telfer (1986–?)]]
**Great-grandchildren:** Levi, Zabella

---

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|----------|------|
| **Mother** | Caroline Edna Lawrie (1890–1957) |
| **Father** | William Henry Parker |
| **Spouse** | [[Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)]] (m. ~1950s) |
| **Children** | [[Daryll William Telfer]], [[John Robert Telfer]], [[Grantley Keith Telfer]], [[Timothy Neil Telfer (1959–?)]], [[Kathryn Mavis Telfer (1961–1965)]] (deceased), [[Susan Shirley Lawrie|Susan Shirley Lawrie]] (adopted) |
| **Siblings** | Avis Muriel (Parker) Nicholls, Howard Lindsay Parker, Sydney Hugh Parker, William Humphrey Parker |

---

## Life Summary

Shirley Edna Telfer (née Parker) was the matriarch of the Telfer family — wife of [[Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)]] for over 50 years, and mother of six children. She spent her life on the family farm in the Ungarra/Tumby Bay region of South Australia's Eyre Peninsula.

Her parents were **William Henry Parker** and **Caroline Edna Lawrie**, who married on 29 March 1917 at Long Plains, South Australia. Caroline Edna was the daughter of Robert Dunlop Lawrie and Caroline Hosking, connecting Shirley to the **Lawrie family** — Scottish pioneers who emigrated from Ayrshire to South Australia in the 1850s and helped establish the Alma Church of Christ.

Shirley raised her family in a strong Christian home. The Church of Christ was central to the Telfer family's life — Murray served as an elder and secretary at both Ungarra and Tumby Bay Churches of Christ for decades, and Shirley was a steadfast partner in that faith journey.

She passed away peacefully at Tumby Bay Hospital on Thursday, 23 February 2017, aged 87. Her funeral was held at the Church of Christ, Tumby Bay, on Wednesday, 1 March 2017, followed by burial at Tumby Bay Cemetery. In lieu of flowers, the family requested donations to the Tumby Bay Hospital Auxiliary.

---

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| 28 Mar 1929 | Born to William Henry Parker and Caroline Edna Lawrie |
| ~1917 | Parents married at Long Plains, SA |
| ~1950s | Married [[Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)]] |
| ~1950s–80s | Raised six children on the family farm, Ungarra area |
| ~1950s–2000s | Active alongside Murray in Ungarra and Tumby Bay Churches of Christ |
| 23 Feb 2017 | Passed away peacefully at Tumby Bay Hospital, aged 87 |
| 1 Mar 2017 | Funeral service at Church of Christ, Tumby Bay; buried at Tumby Bay Cemetery |

- **Funeral Notice** — *Centralian Advocate*, 25 February 2017: Funeral conducted at Church of Christ, Tumby Bay, 1 March 2017 at 11:00am. Cortege proceeded to Tumby Bay Cemetery. Donations to Tumby Bay Hospital Auxiliary.

[View](https://www.carnamah.com.au/bio/alberta-grace-lawrie) — accessed 23 May 2026

---

## Family Connections

- **Parker family:** [[William Henry Parker (1893–1968)]] (father, born Long Plains SA 1893) and Caroline Edna Lawrie (mother). Shirley had four siblings: Avis, Howard Lindsay, Sydney Hugh, and William Humphrey. The Parker line traces back to [[William Humphrey Parker (1850–1926)]] (1850–1926) and [[David Parker (1822–1888)]] (1822–1888), Scottish immigrants from Ayrshire who arrived in SA in 1852.
- **Lawrie family:** Her mother [[Caroline Edna Lawrie (1890–1957)]] profile needed (1890–1957) was the daughter of Robert Dunlop Lawrie and Caroline Hosking. Edna's sister was Alberta Grace "Gracie" Lawrie, whose grandson is **Graham Carslake** (author of the Lawrie family history).
- **Telfer connection:** Through her marriage to Murray John Telfer, she joined one of the pioneering farming families of the Ungarra district — the Telfers arrived on Eyre Peninsula around 1905.

Married at Prospect Church of Christ, captured in the car after the ceremony — Shirley in her veil, pearls, and round glasses, beaming; Murray in his dark suit with boutonnière, content. A joyous new beginning.*

Shirley in her lace-trimmed satin gown, sheer veil secured by a cap headpiece, round dark-rimmed glasses, and delicate necklace with dark pendant, beaming with prominent dimples. # Shirley Edna Telfer (née Parker)

**Born:** 28 March 1929
**Died:** 23 February 2017 (aged 87) — Tumby Bay Hospital, South Australia
**Burial:** Tumby Bay Cemetery, Tumby Bay SA
**Grandson:** [[Mark Kenneth Telfer (1986–?)]]
**Great-grandchildren:** Levi, Zabella

---

## Family

| Relation | Name |

| **Siblings** | Avis Muriel (Parker) Nicholls, Howard Lindsay Parker, Sydney Hugh Parker, William Humphrey Parker |

---

## Life Summary

Shirley Edna Telfer (née Parker) was the matriarch of the Telfer family — wife of [[Murray John Telfer (1924–2009)]] for over 50 years, and mother of six children. She spent her life on the family farm in the Ungarra/Tumby Bay region of South Australia's Eyre Peninsula.

Her parents were **William Henry Parker** and **Caroline Edna Lawrie**, who married on 29 March 1917 at Long Plains, South Australia. Caroline Edna was the daughter of Robert Dunlop Lawrie and Caroline Hosking, connecting Shirley to the **Lawrie family** — Scottish pioneers who emigrated from Ayrshire to South Australia in the 1850s and helped establish the Alma Church of Christ.

Shirley raised her family in a strong Christian home. The Church of Christ was central to the Telfer family's life — Murray served as an elder and secretary at both Ungarra and Tumby Bay Churches of Christ for decades, and Shirley was a steadfast partner in that faith journey.

She passed away peacefully at Tumby Bay Hospital on Thursday, 23 February 2017, aged 87. Her funeral was held at the Church of Christ, Tumby Bay, on Wednesday, 1 March 2017, followed by burial at Tumby Bay Cemetery. In lieu of flowers, the family requested donations to the Tumby Bay Hospital Auxiliary.

---

Sophia March was born in Aylsham, Norfolk, England in March 1829, the third child of **[[Joseph March (1797–1883)]]** and **Sophia Webster**.

On 31 July 1846, at age 17, she arrived in the Colony of South Australia with her parents and **seven siblings** aboard the ship **Canton**. Her father was an agricultural labourer seeking opportunity in the new colony.

She married **[[William John Baker (1831–1919)]]** on 9 March 1853 in Adelaide, at age 23. They settled in the Gawler Plains / Peachy Belt district and raised nine children.

Sophia died on 1 December 1901 in Hyde Park, Adelaide, at age 72, and is buried at West Terrace Cemetery.

---

## Family Origins — The March Line from Norfolk

The March family were from **Aylsham, Norfolk, England** — deep East Anglian farming country. Her father [[Joseph March (1797–1883)]] was born there in 1797. Grandfather Joseph March (abt 1767–1831) was also from Aylsham.

**The family sailed to South Australia on the *Canton*, arriving 31 Jul 1846.** This was part of the wave of English free settlers who helped build the young colony.

# Susan Burton Telfer

**Born:** 1844 | **Died:** 7 Oct 1924 (Yahl, SA) | **Spouse:** [[Robert Telfer (1835–1907)]]

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|---|---|
| Self | [[Susan Burton Telfer (1844–1924)]] |
| Spouse | [[Robert Telfer (1835–1907)]] |

## Life Summary

Susan Burton married Robert Telfer and settled in the Mount Gambier district of South Australia. Her husband Robert worked as stock manager at Moorak, one of the large pastoral estates near Mount Gambier. When Dr. Browne subdivided the Woodlands estate, Robert purchased a farm there and the family moved to that property at Yahl, near Mount Gambier.

They raised seven children — three sons and four daughters. Susan was widowed in 1907 when Robert died, but she continued living on the Woodlands property until her death.

Her obituary in the Border Watch (Mount Gambier, 7 Oct 1924) described her as "another old and highly respected resident of this district." The funeral was conducted by Rev. A. H. Ballinger, with Mr. W. Pearce carrying out the arrangements.

## Timeline

|---|---|
| 1844 | Born |
| ~1860s–1870s | Married Robert Telfer |

| 14 Jan 1907 | Husband Robert died |
| 7 Oct 1924 | Died at Yahl, near Mount Gambier, SA |
| Oct 1924 | Buried at Lake Terrace Cemetery, Mount Gambier |

## Newspaper References

**"MRS. S. TELFER" — Border Watch, Mount Gambier, 7 October 1924**

> Another old and highly respected resident of this district in the person of Mrs. Susan Telfer, of Yahl, passed away on Sunday last. The deceased lady was the wife of the late Mr. Robert Telfer, who for many years was employed on Moorak as stock manager. When Dr. Browne cut up Woodlands Mr. Telfer purchased a farm there and when he retired from Moorak he went there to reside with his family. Mr. Telfer died several years ago, but Mrs. Telfer continued to reside on the property until her death. Mrs. Telfer had a family of seven—three sons and four daughters. The sons are Messrs. Jas., Mount Gambier; W., Yahl; and Robert, N.S.W. The daughters are Mesdames George B. Renfrey, St. Kilda; Rowbotham, North Adelaide; and the Misses S. and E. Telfer. There are several grandchildren. The funeral was held this afternoon, the Rev. A. H. Ballinger conducted the service, and Mr. W. Pearce carried out the funeral arrangements.

**Source:** [Trove – Border Watch, 7 Oct 1924](https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/77719424) — accessed 9 June 2026

# Susannah Sarah Good (1853–1937)

**Born:** 11 Apr 1853, Finniss, South Australia | **Died:** 3 Sep 1937, St Peters, South Australia | **Buried:** Payneham Cemetery, Payneham South, SA | **Father:** Jephthah Good | **Spouse:** [[John Lawrie (1845–1921)]]

## Life Summary

Susannah Sarah Good was born 11 April 1853 at Finniss, South Australia, daughter of Jephthah Good. She married John Lawrie on 16 January 1872 at her father's home near Strathalbyn, SA.

Susannah and John had eleven children, born between 1872 and 1893. The family lived at Alma Plains, Dalkey, and later St Peters (Adelaide). Their daughter Naomi Jubilee died of diphtheria in 1894 aged just 6, a tragedy the family carried.

After John's death in 1921, Susannah survived him for 16 years. She died on 3 September 1937 at St Peters and was buried at Payneham Cemetery, Payneham South.

## Notes

- Finniss is a locality approximately 10 km south of Strathalbyn in South Australia.
- Her father Jephthah Good's home "near Strathalbyn" was the wedding venue in January 1872.
- Her husband's name is recorded in marriage registration as John Lawrie, farmer of Alma Plains.
